name: Misty Rose
lede: Misty Rose is a very pale pink, a screen color from the X11 and CSS lists.

sections.title: A list name
sections.body:
Misty Rose is a color in the X11 Color Set and a CSS keyword, `mistyrose` [1][2]. Paterson's index files it among the pinks next to [[rose]] shades such as magnolia and old rose [1]. The origin of the name is undocumented in our books [1].

The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 lists this swatch's position as "pale pink" (block 31), 3.4 CIEDE2000 units away, and the nearest name in our learning set is baby pink, 9.4 away [3]. Other names near it in the library include Rose Pearl and Zephyr, which Maerz and Paul first recorded in 1920 [3]. The closest article-length neighbor is [[lavender-blush]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our 23,781-painting archive a color near this one appears in 20 paintings, 0.08% of the total, as photographed [4]. In 70% of the 10 paintings where the within-painting lens finds it, it plays a light [4]. The earliest dated match is a Bronzino of 1551, which is far earlier than any record of the name, so this is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph and not proof of a pigment [4]. In printed English the phrase peaks in the 2010s [5].

origin.named_after: origin undocumented; an entry in the X11 color list
origin.source: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour, p. 266

openers: A Bronzino of 1551 contains a color near Misty Rose, but that proves nothing about a pigment: it is a look-alike hue in a photograph.
